title: Nessa and Quinlan's Sparkly Surprise
markdown:
Gadzooks, the Sunspike Peaks were always breezy. When the sun hit the tops just right, they looked like bright golden spikes, sharp and glittering. Nessa, a young witch with hair the colour of a fiery sunset, lived in a crooked little cottage perched on one of these peaks, chimney puffing wisps that smelled of honey and magic. Her very best friend was Quinlan, a goat with whiskers so long they tickled his knees, twitching with a great deal of curiosity. Quinlan was, to put it mildly, very, very interested in everything.

One crisp morning Nessa hummed and stirred a pot that smelled suspiciously like blueberry muffins and a tiny puff of dragon’s breath. From the garden: urgent excited bleats. Baa-baa-BAAA! Not worried. A discovery-alert bleat.

She wiped her hands, peeked out. Quinlan was in a flurry near the gnarled old oak, snowy whiskers vibrating, nose glued to the ground. “What is it, Quinlan?” Then she saw it too. A tiny shimmering crumb, no bigger than a ladybug, like a speck of fallen star. Beside it, a feather of the most unusual luminous sky-blue. Further on, a smear of moss glittering with captured dewdrops, as if dusted with diamond powder.

Quinlan nudged the sparkling moss. Soft inquisitive Baa-baa-bah.

“Crumbs, a sky-blue feather, and sparkly moss all in a line. A very interesting puzzle.”

A happy hop, tail flick. Baa. When Nessa said adventure, good things followed.

The trail wound down from gentle slopes into the dappled shade of the Whispering Woods: pine needles, damp earth, hidden wildflowers. Deeper than they had ever gone. Trees with bark as soft and wrinkled as velvet. Flowers that seemed to hum, petals swaying. Quinlan trotted ahead, excellent nose for the extraordinary. Nessa stepped over gnarled roots that curled like sleeping serpents.

The trail ended at a large gently sloping mossy mound. Nestled among giant sleepy sunflowers, heads drooping as if in thought, a figure so enormous he seemed part of the earth: Gorok the ogre gardener. Mossy green head almost lost in the leafy canopy. Snoring, a rumble like distant gentle thunder. Around him: more crumbs, more blue feathers, clumps of sparkling moss.

Nessa tiptoed. “Excuse me?”

Gorok stirred like a mountain waking. Kind eyes the colour of warm damp soil. A yawn like a gentle avalanche. Mossy beard a thriving ecosystem for tiny wildflowers. “Oh. Hello there. Did I drop something?”

Quinlan nudged a crumb. Questioning Baa-baa-hmmm.

A slow smile. “My sleepy moss soup ingredients. For my prize-winning Moonbeam Marigolds. They need a special treat. The crumbs are from my morning star-fruit scone—very filling. The feathers from the Sky-Whisper birds—rare, the softest touch. And the moss is the most important bit.” A large clump pulsed with inner light. “It makes everything grow with a little extra sparkle and dreaminess.”

Nessa giggled. “Sleepy moss soup for flowers. The most wonderful idea.”

Gorok’s shoulders slumped. “I seem to have misplaced my very special moonpetal bloom. It goes in last, for a dreamy scent that helps the flowers sleep soundly. Without it, the marigolds might just wilt.” Cheeks drooping like petals.

Nessa’s eyes lit. “Moonpetal blooms. They only open on the highest quietest ledges on the northern side of Sunspike. Little silver bells. They shimmer when the moon is full.”

Quinlan bounced. Baa-baa-BAA. He knew those ledges. Tough silvery grass.

“The climb—my legs are a bit too un-nimble. More for sturdy flat ground.”

“That’s no problem.” A small sturdy basket from her pocket, which seemed to hold more than it reasonably should. “Quinlan and I can go. We know the way perfectly.”

They scampered back up the breezy slopes, Quinlan’s whiskers a compass toward the northern ledges. Cooler air. Wind through rocky outcrops, rustling Nessa’s fiery hair. Soon: a cluster of delicate silver-bell flowers, inner light catching sunbeams like tiny diamonds.

Gently she gathered a few, petals cool and soft, into the basket. Quinlan nudged her hand, a rumbling baa of approval, and sniffed to make sure they smelled just right.

Before heading back they sat on a smooth sun-warmed rock. Clouds drifted like fluffy sheep. Quinlan nibbled silvery grass, whiskers twitching. The wind sang through the peaks, wild thyme and distant pine. A breath held in the heart of the mountains.

At Gorok’s sunflower patch a large earthenware pot already bubbled with an earthy aroma. Nessa poured the moonpetals in. A wondrous dreamy scent: slumbering wishes, captured starlight. Gorok stirred with a wooden ladle as big as a small canoe.

“It smells divine.” A little soup onto a particularly droopy Moonbeam Marigold. Instantly the flower stretched, petals unfurling, glowing with a soft silvery light brighter than before.

Happy thunder. He offered Nessa a warm star-fruit scone. “Thank you, little witch. And thank you, whiskered friend.”

Quinlan enjoyed his crumb immensely, whiskers working overtime, a contented almost-purr of goat satisfaction.

Sun descending, hues of orange, pink, and deep purple, long golden shadows across the land. They waved goodbye. Gorok was happily tending his glowing marigolds. The climb home: the breeze on Sunspike a little softer now, a gentle caress carrying the faint sweet scent of moonpetals and the lingering memory of a trail that was not on any dusty old map, only waiting for a curious witch and her wonderfully nosy goat. Nessa’s heart was warm and full. Quinlan’s whiskers still held a crumb of scone, which was, in its way, a kind of map.
